---
title: "Quiz · Hands"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. What distinguishes Mind from Hands?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **Mind** determines *should I do this?*; the **Hands** determine *how do
I do this?*.
:::

## 2. Why are Hands provider-neutral (capability-based)?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
So the Pico depends on capabilities like `email.send` rather than a
provider's tool names like `GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL`. The provider can then be
swapped without changing Pico behaviour or rules.
:::

## 3. What is the fundamental security rule for Hands?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No Hand acts without identity and authorization context. A valid credential
does not imply authorization.
:::

## 4. How are Hands different from MCP?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Hands are the Pico capability abstraction; MCP is an integration mechanism
through which tools may be discovered or executed; Composio is a
provider/platform. These concerns remain separate.
:::

## 5. Name the seven concerns of a Hand invocation and who owns each.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
1. **Composer equipment** — Composer.
2. **Pico decision** — the Pico Mind.
3. **Policy authorization** — Open Engineering rules.
4. **Hand selection** — the Pico runtime.
5. **Provider execution** — the provider (local, Kubernetes, Composio, …).
6. **Evidence** — Pico memory.
7. **Action event** — the Pico Voice.
:::

## 6. Why are **evidence** and the **action event** kept as separate artefacts?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Evidence is a retainable, verifiable record of *what actually happened*,
stored by the Pico so it can be audited or reasoned about later. The action
event is a broadcast on the Pico's Voice so *other participants* can
subscribe and react. One serves memory and accountability; the other
serves distributed communication. Collapsing them removes either
auditability or reach.
:::

## 7. In this wave, is Composio a runnable dependency of the lesson?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No. Composio (and every other external SaaS provider) is illustrative only
in this wave. No exercise, lab step, or verification command contacts an
external service, and no credentials are required. Every runnable check
operates on local YAML using provider-neutral capabilities.
:::
